x: ABOVE: Andrew Lloyd has provided a great boost to our Middle Distance Squad. He followed up his exciting victory in the Commonwealth 5000m with a string of P.b's including a new Oz record for the 3000m with a 7:45.95 effort which erased the long standing time set by Ron Clarke.

Oliver Foote has had one of his best ever points score for our British and achieved a long held ambition to win the Surrey 5000m title to add to the 10000m wins achieved several years ago. Here he leads a classy Div.1 BAL field with Andrew Lloyd just behind him .
Following a tremendous track season Andrew Lloyd has returned home for an enforced break. He will be having another foot operation to remove bone injured several years ago in a car accident.

Paul Evans astounded everyone by running the fastest long leg by a 20 sec. margin while Andy Lloyd made a welcome return to finish 2nd fastest on the short leg followed by Justin Chaston 3rd fastest and a somewhat surprised Stuart Paton in 6th fastest place on the short leg.
Sprint Relay 4x100m : 1st England (With Marcus and John) 38.67(Games Record) 5000m : 1st Andrew Lloyd 13:24.86.

Advised by former Belgravian Graham Seatter, who was working on the TV commentaries, he did a great job only losing it on the final day as Gary Staines and Andy Lloyd paraded it at the Closing Ceremony.
Best performance of the day came from Andy Lloyd, who front ran the 1500 and left everybody for dead as he stretched out a very high class field.

Our middle distance men rallied well with Darryl Maynard standing in at 20 minutes notice to gain good 800 m points while we won both 1500m's with Stuart Paton gaining a faster win in the 'B' than Andy LLoyd in 'A' - but Andy then ran the 'A' 5000 some 30 minutes later to record a very creditable 14.04.
News of our Commonwealth 5,000 metre Champion Andy Lloyd: back on 28th April he placed 7th in 29:30 in a 10k road race in Borobudur, Java, an event won by Abebe of Ethiopia in 27:43.
Australia's Commonwealth Champion, Andy Lloyd, was in heat 3 but he never really got stuck into the race, winding up 9th although just a second down on Gary's time.
